page.notes: The "6" and the small marks at the top right are handwriting or stamps, not printed text, and are left out. The last left-column line is cut off at the bottom edge and only its first words are legible. The Greek heading word is uncertain, so it is marked [?]. Left-hand lines "est, jingulare est" and "necesse est esse" are doubtful in part; "jingulare" may be "singulare". The "a" in "Oppositia" and "actu" is read from a ligatured form and is doubtful. "acres" at the end of "Orationes perinde vera sunt acres" is doubtful.
